Elena to prepare controls mapping doc for encryption/KMS and VPC options
Schedule technical deep dive for Dedicated/Private deployment (SE-led)
Customer to share data residency and retention policy details
action_items: Samir Patel: Share SOC 2 Type II PDF + link to trust center by 2026-11-02
Elena Zhao: Produce controls mapping (Redwood controls -> ISO27001/SOC2) by 2026-11-06
Mark Rivera: Send data residency and retention requirements by 2026-11-04
Aisha Khan: Confirm acceptable data residency regions and compliance docs needed by 2026-11-05
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-30
Time: 15:00 PST - 15:42 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Zhao (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Redwood CSM), Laura Kim (Edenwell CISO), Mark Rivera (Edenwell Head of Infra), Aisha Khan (Edenwell Legal), Tom Ellis (Edenwell App Owner)
summary: Customer wanted an end-to-end posture review: access to SOC 2/ISO artifacts, mapping of Redwood controls to their compliance matrix, and specifics on encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and data residency for a pilot. Redwood AE/SE confirmed Trust Center access, SOC2 Type II availability, and proposed controls mapping + a follow-up technical deep dive for Dedicated/Private deployment options.
topics: SOC 2 Type II availability and scope
Trust Center access and shared artifacts
Encryption at rest and in transit + KMS options
Audit logs retention and delivery (SIEM integration)
Data residency and regional hosting options
references: SOC2 Type II (shared drive link) - redwood/soc2/2026-type2.pdf
Controls mapping template (Google Sheet) - shared during call
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through Redwood's SOC 2 / ISO posture and then dive into the specific controls you asked about. Laura, you had a couple prefixed items on the agenda, want to kick us off?
[00:18] Laura Kim: Yeah hi, thanks Samir. Quick background - Edenwell is starting a pilot that handles PHI-adjacent data, so security and residency are must-haves. We're mostly evaluating whether Redwood hosted API is sufficient or if we need Dedicated or Private. Main asks: SOC2 scope, ISO alignment, KMS options, SSO/RBAC, and audit logs.
[00:35] Samir Patel: Great, that matches what we have. Elena will cover the technical bits - KMS, audit logs, RBAC - and I'll follow with compliance artifacts and next steps.
[00:48] Elena Zhao: Hi all - quick intro, I'm Elena, I run infra integrations on the SE team. We'll try to be concrete about what we can provide out of the box vs what needs dedicated deployment.
[01:05] Tom Ellis: Apologies, jumping in - timeline wise we're aiming for a pilot in Jan, so we need to know blockers.
[01:20] Mark Rivera: Yes, and we have to map Redwood controls into our ISO 27001 matrix, also need how you handle KMS key custody.
[01:30] Elena Zhao: On SOC 2 - Redwood has a Type II that covers hosted API and core infra controls, encryption in transit and at rest, access controls, change management. For keys we offer two patterns: Redwood-managed KMS (default) and customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private deployments. For Dedicated there is also an option to bring your own KMS depending on the contract.
[01:55] Laura Kim: Can you spell out the difference - customer-managed in Dedicated vs Private? I.e., are keys fully isolated?
[02:10] Elena Zhao: In Private (VPC/on-prem) you control the KMS and we do not have the plaintext - it's customer side. For Dedicated, keys can be customer-controlled if we deploy a customer KMS in their dedicated environment but there's still a network path; we can provide guidance for HSM-backed KMS. The hosted default uses Redwood KMS, but we log all key usage in audit logs.
[02:36] Samir Patel: Also note our Trust Center contains the SOC2 report and control narratives. I'll share the link after the call.
[02:42] Aisha Khan: We need to review the control narratives for encryption, personnel background checks, and vendor management. Also, any subprocessor list?
[02:54] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a subprocessors list in the trust center. I'll include that.
[03:10] Elena Zhao: On RBAC and SSO: Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with fine-grained route-level permissions in the console; API tokens can be scoped and rotated.
[03:32] Mark Rivera: For audit logging, can you stream logs to our SIEM? We want event-level logs for auth, keys, and request metadata for 12 months.
[03:45] Elena Zhao: We support log forwarding to customer SIEMs (S3, syslog, or direct API integrations). Hosted customers can request retention windows; for long-term retention we recommend log export to your S3. Some retention levels are add-ons.
[04:05] Laura Kim: Does Redwood provide attestation for change management or patching cadence for the runtime?
[04:12] Samir Patel: Yes - change management and patching cadence are in the SOC 2 docs and we can provide summary notes. Our uptime SLA and scheduled maintenance cadence are in the contract.
[04:27] Tom Ellis: On data residency - we need keys and data to remain in US east or Canada, depends on the dataset. Do you offer region pinning?
[04:40] Elena Zhao: We do regional routing and can pin to specific regions for Dedicated and Private. Hosted can be regionally isolated in certain clouds/regions, but for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[04:57] Laura Kim: For the controls mapping, we need a template showing Redwood control -> ISO 27001 clause -> evidence (doc/link). Can you do that?
[05:08] Samir Patel: Yes. Elena will create a mapping doc mapping our controls to SOC2 criteria and ISO 27001 clauses, and link to supporting evidence in the Trust Center.
[05:20] Elena Zhao: We'll also annotate where evidence is a policy vs an operational artifact (e.g., patch logs, vulnerability scans, change tickets).
[05:32] Mark Rivera: A few nitty gritty items - network isolation, public endpoints, and KV cache handling. We need to understand whether any cached tokens or KV caches might leak across tenants.
[05:45] Elena Zhao: Good question - our runtime uses tenant isolation and KV cache is scoped per-tenant. There's a risk model for shared hosts which we address via strict tenancy separation and quotas; for extra assurance Dedicated gives you dedicated pools so no shared tenancy.
[06:05] Laura Kim: Can you provide the control that explains tenancy isolation?
[06:10] Samir Patel: Yes, that's in the security architecture doc in the Trust Center. I'll point it out in the link I send.
[06:20] Aisha Khan: On legal - we need to see Data Processing Agreement (DPA) language supporting PHI handling. Is there an addendum?
[06:30] Samir Patel: We have a DPA and BAAs are evaluated case-by-case; for PHI-adjacent pilot we can discuss BAA options. I'll loop in legal after this call.
[06:44] Tom Ellis: One more - retention of request/response bodies. We can't have long-term retention of sensitive outputs unless explicit. What's Redwood's default?
[06:56] Elena Zhao: Default is short-lived request logs with redaction for secrets; customers can enable longer retention but it's opt-in and often tied to Dedicated/Private or enterprise add-on. Hosted has configurable retention windows. We'll provide the exact retention numbers in the follow-up.
[07:20] Laura Kim: Are there penetration test or vuln reports we can see?
[07:28] Samir Patel: We have third-party pentest summaries and internal vuln management artifacts - redacted pentest reports are in the trust center. Full reports may require an NDA.
[07:42] Mark Rivera: For SSO integration, we use Okta and Azure AD. Any gotchas for SCIM provisioning?
[07:50] Elena Zhao: Both are supported. Provisioning works via SCIM, and SAML SSO in our console. We recommend testing in a staging tenant first.
[08:05] Laura Kim: Can you clarify the log fields you provide in the audit stream? We need user, action, resource, timestamp, IP, and request metadata including model used and token counts.
[08:18] Elena Zhao: Yes we include user/action/resource/timestamp/IP, and we can include request metadata (model, tokens) as optional fields. Token-level details may be redacted depending on retention and privacy settings.
[08:35] Samir Patel: To call out one concern we hear often - encryption key custody. For a lot of customers, default Redwood-managed KMS is fine but for regulated data they want customer-managed KMS; we support that path.
[08:52] Laura Kim: Ok that helps. Regarding ISO 27001, do you have a formal ISMS scope or certification?
[09:02] Samir Patel: Redwood is aligning to ISO 27001 and has many controls mapped; some customers have asked for a formal cert - it's in roadmap and we can provide mapping/compensating controls in the meantime.
[09:20] Aisha Khan: How about audit logs for admin-level console actions? We need to see role changes, user provisioning, and API key rotations.
[09:30] Elena Zhao: Those are included in admin audit logs and we can export them. For Dedicated/Private customers we can also set up push-based exports to their SIEM.
[09:44] Tom Ellis: Any limitations on API token scoping? We want tokens that only allow embeddings but not generation and vice versa.
[09:54] Elena Zhao: We support scoped tokens and route-level permissions. You can create tokens scoped to embeddings vs generation and limit by model.
[10:10] Laura Kim: Let's talk about evidence for personnel controls - background checks, separation of duties.
[10:18] Samir Patel: Those are covered in HR policies; we include narratives and attestations in SOC 2. If you need redacted evidence we can identify what we can share.
[10:30] Mark Rivera: On network egress - are there egress rules that could send data to third parties or subprocessors we should be aware of?
[10:40] Elena Zhao: Subprocessors are listed; outbound calls from the runtime are controlled and audited. We'll include subprocessors list in the trust center package.
[10:55] Laura Kim: For the controls mapping, can you produce a table that maps Redwood control, evidence link, control owner, and how that maps to our ISO clauses?
[11:05] Elena Zhao: Yes - we'll populate that table and indicate where evidence is gated by NDA.
[11:20] Samir Patel: Quick interjection - you mentioned timeline for pilot in Jan, we'll aim to have mapping and SOC docs to you in early November so you can complete legal review.
[11:33] Aisha Khan: That timeline works but we might need to schedule legal-to-legal call.
[11:40] Samir Patel: We'll do that if needed after we share docs.
[11:48] Mark Rivera: A few technical follow-ups for Elena: 1) Can you provide sample SIEM mapping for log fields? 2) KMS key rotation process and frequency? 3) For Dedicated, what's the network topology template?
[12:05] Elena Zhao: I'll prepare samples: syslog/S3 export mapping, key rotation docs (we rotate keys regularly and customer-managed keys follow customer's rotation policy), and a network topology template we use for Dedicated customers.
[12:25] Tom Ellis: Are there benchmarking or performance guarantees that change with Dedicated v Hosted? We need latency SLOs for the pilot.
[12:36] Samir Patel: Dedicated gives more predictable throughput and latency SLOs; hosted is best-effort with published performance profiles. We'll attach the perf profiles and the Dedicated SLAs in the follow-up.
[12:50] Laura Kim: Any compliance packages or add-ons we should know about?
[12:56] Samir Patel: Yes - longer log retention, expanded audit exports, and dedicated support tiers are add-ons. We'll enumerate costs in the pricing follow-up.
[13:10] (Speaker 1): 
[13:25] Aisha Khan: On DPA and BAA - can you send redlined language or is it standard?
[13:34] Samir Patel: We typically provide a standard DPA and can discuss BAA specifics; legal can take it from there.
[13:47] Mark Rivera: For the controls mapping, please call out any gaps where Redwood's current posture doesn't map directly to ISO clause and recommend compensating controls.
[13:58] Elena Zhao: We'll mark gaps and recommended mitigations.
[14:10] Tom Ellis: Ok, sounds good. Any other security concerns from the team?
[14:18] Laura Kim: One - do you do customer-facing key escrow for keys used in models or any derivatives?
[14:28] Elena Zhao: We do not escrow customer keys; customer-managed keys remain under customer control. For hosted Redwood-managed keys we manage rotation and don't escrow plain text.
[14:40] Samir Patel: I'll flag the parts of the SOC 2 that speak to key management in the notes I share.
[14:50] Maya Torres: I'll coordinate the doc share and follow-up meeting scheduling.
[15:00] Laura Kim: Thanks. A couple of items for us: we'll send a short list of required artifacts and a contacts list for legal and infra.
[15:12] Samir Patel: Perfect. We'll aim to deliver the SOC2 PDF, trust center link, and the initial controls mapping by the dates discussed.
[15:25] Elena Zhao: For the technical deep dive we'll propose two time slots next week and include a Dedicated topology example.
[15:36] Mark Rivera: One more question about encryption: do you encrypt model weights at rest differently than customer data?
[15:44] Elena Zhao: Model weights are encrypted at rest with platform-managed keys; customer data encryption is separate and can be customer-managed. We'll call out the distinction in the mapping.
[15:58] Tom Ellis: That's clear.
[16:05] Laura Kim: Ok let's recap.
[16:10] Samir Patel: Recap: 1) Samir share SOC2 Type II and trust center link; 2) Elena prepare controls mapping + technical artifacts (SIEM mapping, KMS rotation docs, Dedicated topology); 3) Customer share residency/retention reqs and legal contacts; 4) Schedule technical deep dive. Any objections?
[16:35] Aisha Khan: No objections.
[16:38] Laura Kim: Looks good.
[16:42] Samir Patel: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with links and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[16:50] (call ends)
notes: Follow-up actions centered on sending SOC2 and trust center access, controls mapping for ISO/SOC mapping, and scheduling an SE-led technical deep dive. Customer emphasized PHI-adjacent constraints, region pinning, and KMS custody. Possible legal-to-legal discussion (BAA).
